message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most rural roads, 35 mph on most urban roads.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• “No Speed Limit” signs are rare; if none, use the posted limit. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all ages. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs give priority to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• “Lane‑change” rules apply on highways and multi‑lane roads. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a ticket. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – Vehicle Registration | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway).
• Use electronic toll tags (e‑Tag) or pay at toll plazas. | TxDOT – Toll Roads | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Winter & Weather Conditions** | • Use winter tires or chains in certain counties during snow/ice.
• Adjust driving to weather conditions. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | | **Penalties & Fines** | • Fines vary by offense; DUI can lead to up to 2 years in jail.
• Points added to driver’s record can lead to license suspension. | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) – Traffic Violations | ### How to Get Official, Up‑to‑Date Information 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TP/htm/TP.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Provides road‑specific rules, speed limits, and construction updates. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/ 3. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Handles registration, licensing, and vehicle inspection requirements. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 4. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Offers information on DUI laws, penalties, and driver’s license status. *Website:* https://www.dps.texas.gov/ 5. **Local County or City Ordinances** – Some municipalities have additional traffic regulations (e.g., parking restrictions, speed limits). Check your city’s official website. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid tickets. - **Use hands‑free devices** – stay compliant with cell‑phone laws. - **Be mindful of school zones** – speeds drop significantly near schools. - **Plan for weather** – Texas can have sudden storms; adjust speed and following distance. If you need more detailed information on a specific topic (e.g., DUI penalties, school bus rules, or toll road payment methods), let me know!
